section: Iterate — change: mark two Semgrep false positives
title: Suppress the remaining two Semgrep findings as false positives
context: After the 2026-10-23 security fixes, semgrep --config auto still reported two findings. One was a non-literal RegExp in the lookup service's origin check. The other was a script-tag pattern in a test that checks the static index.html.
decision: Each finding gets a justification comment plus a nosemgrep comment directly above the matched line. The origin regex is built only from escaped deployment config and is covered by lookalike-origin tests. The test only asserts on file text.
consequences: The Semgrep scan is clean, so any new finding shows up. A future change that feeds request data into that RegExp would no longer be flagged at this line.
rationale: Both findings were confirmed false positives by spec and code review. Rewriting working, tested code just to satisfy the scanner would add risk for no gain.
rejected: Replacing the regex with string checks: more code that reimplements already-tested behaviour.
